land.text: Teng, 'annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC'; its territory 'corresponds to present-day Tengzhou'

successors.note: The page also says Yue conquered Teng in 414 (infobox 'Conquered by Yue: 414 BCE'; lead '1046-414 BC'); see the ledger.

capitals.name: Teng (Tengzhou)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Tengzhou'; the page puts Teng 'in the south of modern-day Shandong province'. Coordinates are modern Tengzhou.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape plus the capital area round Tengzhou, carried back to 1046

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's first Teng shape: 'Established: 1046 BCE', a viscounty founded by Shu Xiu of Cuo, a brother of King Wu. Cliopatria's 750 shape carried back with the capital area added.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape plus a 25 km circle round Tengzhou, valid -750..-298

keyframe_review.note: 4,324 km2 for -750..-481, 116.1-117.2E, 34.7-35.5N. The page makes Tengzhou the capital and says Teng's territory 'corresponds to present-day Tengzhou', but Tengzhou (117.16E) lies on the eastern edge of the shape, which is displaced west of it (and about 3 cells of the Tengzhou circle fall in Cliopatria's Teng, 6 in its Zhu). Correction: the shape plus a 25 km circle round Tengzhou. The infobox has no area, so the size cannot be checked.

correction.text: the same shape, valid -480..-298 until Song annihilated Teng in 297

keyframe_review.note: 4,324 km2 for -480..-451, identical to the earlier shape. Cliopatria ends Teng in 451, but the page has Teng 'annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC' (the Spring and Autumn table: 'Teng 297 BCE: to Song'), after a conquest by Yue in 414 (infobox) that the lead reads as the end of Teng. The shape therefore runs to -298, with the Tengzhou circle added; Cliopatria meanwhile hands 15 of its cells to Song in 450 and 10 to its Xu row, which the page does not support.

region.text: Teng at Tengzhou, in the south of modern Shandong

ledger.note: 1046: the Zhou enfeoff Shu Xiu of Cuo, a brother of King Wu, as viscount of Teng in southern Shandong. Infobox 'Established: 1046 BCE'; capital Tengzhou; 'its territory corresponds to present-day Tengzhou'.

414: Yue conquers Teng. Infobox 'Conquered by Yue: 414 BCE' and lead '1046-414 BC'; the page says King Zhugou of Yue conquered Teng. Teng is nonetheless 'finally annihilated' by Song in 297, so the dossier keeps Teng as a Yue-held state to then; recorded from Teng's side (the land is Teng's, held by Yue).

333: Yue's hold on Teng ends at the latest with the fall of Yue: 'Yue was partitioned by Chu and Qi in 333 BC' (Yue page; infobox 'Conquered by Chu: 333 BC'). No page opened says when Teng recovered or whether Chu or Qi held it; Teng is annihilated by Song in 297 (confidence 1). (Reviewer ea-01-c: moved from 297, which outlived Yue itself.)

297: King Kang of Song annihilates Teng. 'Finally it was annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC'; infobox 'Conquered by Song: 297 BCE'; the Spring and Autumn table 'Teng 297 BCE: to Song'; the Song page says only that Song 'annexed Teng'.

wars.name: Yue conquest of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng conquered by King Zhugou of Yue (414 on the infobox); the page's lead takes 414 as the end of Teng, its text and the Spring and Autumn table keep Teng until 297.
wars.note: Left unsettled; the Yue page was not opened (1-2 page budget).

wars.name: Song annihilation of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng annihilated by King Kang of Song; its land goes to Song.

certainty.note: A small viscounty known by its capital Tengzhou; the frontier with Lu, Zhu, Xue and Song is unsurveyed.

sources.title: Teng (state)
sources.note: Identity, Tengzhou, 1046, Yue 414 and Song 297; no rulers' years, no area.

sources.title: Yue (state)
sources.note: Reviewer ea-01-c: 'Yue was partitioned by Chu and Qi in 333 BC'; infobox 'Conquered by Chu: 333 BC'. Teng is not mentioned.

notes: One dossier for Cliopatria's 'Teng' (-750..-451), extended back to 1046 and forward to 297. The page contradicts itself on the end: lead and infobox give conquest by Yue in 414 ('1046-414 BC'), the text and table give annihilation by Song in 297; the dossier ends in 297 and holds Yue's 414 conquest as an occupation. If the 414 reading is wanted instead, the occupation events and the 297 dissolve change to a dissolve in 414 with successor yue. Cliopatria's Teng shape sits west of Tengzhou and 15 of its cells go to Song and 10 to its Xu row in 450; both are unsupported. The page says Teng was a vassal of Lu (no dates); a vassal_start belongs in the Lu dossier. Gazetteer: Tengzhou is not a gazetteer place (coordinates used); name needed.
